verified_key_information_units.information: The 2025 revenue decline was driven by the completion of major projects initiated in prior years during 2025, combined with a slower pace of new contract signing in 2024 and the first half of 2025; this project cycle effect compressed profitability despite eventual improvement in contract signing activity later in 2025.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Statement of the Chairman of the Management Board: 'In 2024, we were engaged in several large projects that had been started in earlier years, and these were completed as planned during 2025. The pace of signing new contracts was slower in 2024 and in the first half of 2025.'

verified_key_information_units.information: A major improvement in contract signing during the second half of 2025 resulted in the execution of Merko's largest-ever contracts for the Rūdninkai defence campus in Lithuania, which will contribute gradually to revenue starting in 2026 and provide stable workload for years ahead.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Statement of the Chairman of the Management Board: 'the second half of 2025 showed a clear improvement, and preparatory efforts resulted in new major contracts... signing of the largest contracts in Merko’s history for the construction of two phases of the Rūdninkai defence campus... will begin to contribute to revenue gradually in 2026 and onwards.'

candidate_sentences.text: Key forthcoming projects include multi-phase defence facilities in Lithuania, which will phase into revenue streams from 2026 onward.

verified_key_information_units.information: The company expanded its public-private partnership (PPP) business through new real estate development agreements signed in 2025 for the Krulli quarter (Tallinn) and Uus-Karlowa quarter (Tartu), alongside continued success in the Noblessner area, enhancing long-term workload stability and diversification.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Statement of the Chairman of the Management Board: 'Alongside the successful real estate development partnership in the Noblessner area of Tallinn, we signed two similar cooperation agreements in 2025 for the development of the Krulli quarter in Tallinn and the Uus-Karlowa quarter in Tartu. The Rūdninkai project marks a significant expansion of our PPP business Lithuania.'

details.completeness_justification: K1, K3, K5, K7, and K8 are fully represented with supporting sentences. K2 and K4 are missing entirely, as the candidate does not explain the project cycle effect driving the revenue decline or detail the specific public-private partnership expansions. K6 is also missing, as there is no mention of residential construction activity surge, apartment sales figures, or inventory buildup. The overall coverage captures most of the high-importance financial and strategic elements, but the absence of three key criteria (especially K2 which explains the core reason for the decline) prevents the summary from achieving a 'Yes' rating. The main picture is captured, but important contextual and operational details are omitted.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is fully coherent internally. All statements are logically connected and support each other without contradiction. The narrative flows from revenue performance to profitability, balance sheet strength, market conditions, strategic approach, and future outlook. Explanations for changes (e.g., contract completions reducing construction revenue, real estate growth, efficiency driving profits) are clear and consistent. No material logical gaps, contradictions, or organizational problems are present. The summary forms a unified whole with appropriate transitions between topics.
